raw.assessment: The incumbent reliably preserved designs in the observed batch and caught seven fitting problems before dispatch, but required rework and exceeded the time target. Rework clustered in large covers (5/8 versus 2/14 medium and 0/18 small); this supports investigating size-linked fit errors without establishing their cause. Small unadjusted covers taking 25–31 minutes suggest feasible processing times for that subgroup only. The concrete limiting observation is two customer failures on rounded-corner tables: passing the existing reference-table check may not establish customer fit. Wash shrinkage and estimated waste leave further uncertainty; the supplied observations do not establish five-cycle durability or compliance with the area-based waste ceiling.

openings.claim: The common cutting allowance may create a systematic size-dependent fit error that cutting the whole batch propagates before fitting feedback arrives.
openings.delta: Move fitting feedback ahead of repeated cutting and distinguish an allowance error from cutting or sewing variation.
openings.prediction: If the allowance is responsible, large covers cut and sewn accurately to the current card will show a repeatable directional fit error; transfer or sewing errors instead produce discrepancies between planned and achieved dimensions.
openings.probe: Before bulk cutting, complete one ordered cover per size. Record order dimensions, card dimensions, cut dimensions, finished dimensions, fit and stage working times; also record design, cutting direction and operator. Treat this as a screen, then replicate any suspected error before revising the card. Check revised nesting by area before further cuts.
assumptions: Existing tools permit sufficiently accurate measurements.
Sequencing and measurements fit the three-week window and 350-unit budget; no success-rate or median-time improvement is yet established.

openings.claim: Do customer failures arise from rounded corner geometry independently of actual tabletop dimensions?
openings.delta: Test the reference table's representativeness separately from production accuracy.
openings.prediction: A geometry effect predicts corner-pocket interference on rounded tables despite matching measured length and width; dimension mismatch predicts failure tracking dimensional discrepancy instead.
openings.probe: Ask the six willing customers for actual length, width and corner measurements, prioritizing nominal-only orders where possible. Compare first-placement behavior on measured customer tables and reference tables. Use retained offcuts to screen a removable corner-pocket revision if interference persists; test both-direction dimensional change and the stipulated five-cycle wash performance before adoption.
assumptions: Willing customers include informative table geometries and can report placement consistently.
Any adopted revision honors size and design, uses purchased stock, and passes budget, time, wash and area-waste checks.

raw.assessment: A cover that seats correctly despite corner-shape differences and washing would be useful, but the observations do not establish how to achieve it. Rounded-corner installation failures support investigating corner accommodation; they do not explain the separate concentration of seam rework among larger covers.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: a concealed pleated corner pocket, closed with a washable cloth tie preset by the cooperative, could accommodate a measured rounded corner while preserving the ordered visible panel and allowing tool-free removal. The speculative capability is geometry-specific seating without exhibitor readjustment.
openings.delta: Replace fixed corner-pocket geometry with a small preset adjustment reserve. Dependencies are actual corner measurements, sufficient pocket travel after washing, stable tie settings, and a cutting layout that supplies the extra cloth. The presently testable partial capability is repeatable seating of one preset corner pocket.
openings.prediction: Compared with the current pocket, the preset pleated version will seat on a measured rounded corner without resetting its tie, both initially and after the stipulated five-cycle wash test. Failure to improve seating, or tie-setting drift, would count against the mechanism.
openings.probe: Obtain actual dimensions and corner measurements from willing customers, prioritizing nominal-only orders. Use retained offcuts to sew matched current and pleated corner samples. Compare repeated blind placements on the same measured customer corner if access is available; check tie movement, removal, and visible print disturbance before and after washing. Before batch adoption, time a complete pilot and measure the proposed layout waste by area. Proceed only within 350 units, two machines, three weeks, and 8% cutting waste; assess the final 40 against at least 38 first-placement fits, all ordered designs, and median working time at most 32 minutes.
assumptions: A customer can provide corner-test access beyond the offered measurements.
The purchased cloth can form durable, concealed pleats and ties.
Pilot material, preparation, and added sewing fit the resource and delivery limits.

openings.claim: Common allowance may cause size-linked error amplified by bulk cutting.
openings.discriminator: Repeatable directional error despite card conformity versus transfer/sewing discrepancies.
openings.fit: Preserves selections; revised nesting needs area validation.
openings.probe: Complete one ordered cover per size before bulk cutting; record order/card/cut/finished dimensions, fit, stage times, design, direction and operator. Replicate suspected error before card revision.
openings.uncertainty: Measurement adequacy and resource fit unproven; small-cover times do not establish batch performance.

openings.claim: Rounded corners may defeat reference-table fit independently of dimensional mismatch.
openings.discriminator: Corner interference at matching length/width versus failures tracking dimensional discrepancies.
openings.probe: Obtain actual dimensions and corner measurements from six willing customers, prioritizing nominal-only orders; compare customer/reference first placements. Screen removable pocket revisions with offcuts; measure both-direction wash change.
openings.uncertainty: Informative geometries and consistent placement reporting uncertain; current wash evidence lacks width and durability proof.

openings.claim: Concealed pleated pocket with preset washable cloth tie may accommodate measured rounded corners without readjustment.
openings.discriminator: Improved seating versus current pocket after repeated placements and five washes, without tie drift or print disturbance.
openings.fit: Uncertain extra cloth, sewing time and durability.
openings.probe: Compare matched offcut pockets in blind placements on the same customer corner; check removal and tie movement. Time a complete pilot and measure layout waste by area.
openings.uncertainty: Customer test access, cloth suitability and postwash travel unproven; does not explain large-cover rework.

post_distill.decision: Probe before adoption. Preserve ordered sizes/designs and purchased stock; require tool-free removal, five-cycle wash survival, at most 350 units, two machines, three weeks and 8% area waste. Prior weight estimate is insufficient. Evaluate 40 covers: at least 38 first fits, all designs correct, median work at most 32 minutes.
